hints: Look at the three cube sizes and ask yourself, which one will the acid reach the centre of first to turn it fully colourless?
Recall that diffusion rate depends on surface area to volume ratio, calculated as (6 x side x side) divided by (side x side x side) for a cube.
walkthrough:
**Decide which cube finishes first**

Think like the acid. It has to diffuse from the surface to the centre. The smallest cube has the shortest distance to the centre and the largest surface area relative to its volume, so it will become colourless in the least time. That is the $2 \text{ cm} \times 2 \text{ cm} \times 2 \text{ cm}$ cube.

**Calculate surface area and volume**

For any cube of side $l$:
$$\text{surface area} = 6 \times l^2$$
$$\text{volume} = l^3$$
For $l = 2 \text{ cm}$:
$$\text{surface area} = 6 \times 2 \times 2 = 24 \text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{volume} = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8 \text{ cm}^3$$

**Work out the ratio**

Now divide surface area by volume:
$$\text{ratio} = 24 : 8 = 3.0 : 1$$
A larger ratio means faster diffusion, so this confirms the smallest cube is the fastest and the answer is D.

options.A: This is the volume to surface area ratio of the 2 cm cube ($8:24 = 0.33:1$), not surface area to volume. It is upside down.
options.B: This is the volume to surface area ratio of the 5 cm cube ($125:150 = 0.83:1$), not surface area to volume. It is upside down.
options.C: This is the correct surface area to volume ratio for the largest 5 cm cube ($150:125 = 1.2:1$), which would take the longest time, not the least.
options.D: Correct. This is the surface area to volume ratio for the smallest 2 cm cube ($24:8 = 3.0:1$), which has the largest ratio and so becomes colourless fastest.
